quotes.text: It is in fact the cold-blooded nature of his crime that I find most chilling.
quotes.speaker: Prosecutor
quotes.context: The prosecutor closing his case against Andy in front of the Maine jury, framing the circumstantial evidence as proof of premeditation.

quotes.text: I loved her very much. I just wasn't a good husband to her.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy on the stand at his murder trial, attempting to explain the marriage the prosecutor is using against him.

quotes.text: I must admit I didn't think much of Andy first time I laid eyes on him. Looked like a stiff breeze would blow him over.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover as the bus of new arrivals enters Shawshank, introducing Andy as he sees him for the first time.

quotes.text: Fresh fish today! We're reeling them in!
quotes.speaker: Heywood
quotes.context: Heywood and other long-term inmates jeering at the new arrivals as they are walked into the cellblock for the first time.

quotes.text: Fresh fish! Fresh fish!
quotes.speaker: Heywood
quotes.context: Heywood leading the chant as the new prisoners are processed by the guards.

quotes.text: When I say you eat, you eat! When I say you shit, you shit! You got that, you maggot-dick motherfucker?
quotes.speaker: Captain Hadley
quotes.context: Hadley laying down the rules to the new prisoners on their first night, before he beats one of them to death for crying.

quotes.text: You eat when we say you eat, you sleep when we say you sleep.
quotes.speaker: Captain Hadley
quotes.context: Hadley asserting total control over the new prisoners' bodies as part of the induction routine.

quotes.text: Rule number one: no blasphemy. I'll not have the Lord's name taken in vain in my prison.
quotes.speaker: Warden Norton
quotes.context: Norton addressing the new prisoners on their first day, opening with a religious rule rather than a legal one.

quotes.text: The first night's the toughest. No doubt about it.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during the new prisoners' first night, as one of them cries himself into a fatal beating from Hadley.

quotes.text: Everybody's innocent in here. Don't you know that?
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red, sceptical, when Andy maintains his innocence in their first proper conversation in the yard.

quotes.text: I'm a man who knows how to get things.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red explaining his role inside the prison economy when Andy asks how he might obtain a rock hammer.

quotes.text: Why don't you swallow what's in your mouth, then you can talk.
quotes.speaker: Bogs Diamond
quotes.context: Bogs, leader of the Sisters, threatening Andy in the yard early in his sentence.

quotes.text: Mr. Hadley, do you trust your wife?
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy's opening line to Hadley on the licence-plate-factory roof, leading into the tax-free gift advice that earns the work crew their three beers each.

quotes.text: Stinking government, they will fish in your pocket for spare change.
quotes.speaker: Captain Hadley
quotes.context: Hadley complaining on the prison roof about the tax he is about to pay on his inheritance, the complaint Andy uses to buy his crew their beers.

quotes.text: We sat and drank with the sun on our shoulders and felt like free men.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover on the rooftop sequence, summing up what Andy's tax advice bought his crew that morning.

quotes.text: We could have been tarring the roof of one of our own houses.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover continuing the rooftop sequence, framing the men's morning of beer and labour as briefly indistinguishable from ordinary working life.

quotes.text: For the briefest of moments every last man at Shawshank felt free.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during the Mozart broadcast, as the entire prison stops and listens.

quotes.text: That's the beauty of music. They can't get that from you.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy at the lunch table, after his two-week stretch in solitary for playing Mozart over the loudspeakers, defending the broadcast to Red and the others.

quotes.text: There are places in this world that aren't made out of stone. There's something inside that they can't get to, that they can't touch. That's yours.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy explaining hope to Red at the lunch table after the Mozart broadcast.

quotes.text: Hope is a dangerous thing. Hope can drive a man insane.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's reply to Andy in the lunch room after the Mozart scene, warning his friend against the very thing the film will spend the next hour vindicating.

quotes.text: Let me tell you something, my friend. Hope is a dangerous thing.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red preparing his warning to Andy in the same lunch-room exchange, immediately after the Mozart broadcast.

quotes.text: Could you get me Rita Hayworth?
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy asking Red, a few years into his sentence, to obtain a poster of Rita Hayworth, the first of the three pin-ups that will conceal the tunnel.

quotes.text: These walls are funny. First you hate em, then you get used to em. Enough time passes, gets so you depend on them. That's institutionalised.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red explaining institutionalisation to the younger inmates over a meal in the canteen, after Heywood mocks Brooks for threatening Heywood with a knife rather than leave the prison.

quotes.text: They send you here for life and that's exactly what they take. The part that counts, anyway.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red, in the same canteen exchange about Brooks, framing the long sentence as the slow theft of an inner life.

quotes.text: The world went and got itself in a big damn hurry.
quotes.speaker: Brooks Hatlen
quotes.context: Brooks in voiceover, writing his last letter back to the boys at Shawshank from his halfway-house room.

quotes.text: I don't like it here. I'm tired of being afraid all the time. I've decided not to stay.
quotes.speaker: Brooks Hatlen
quotes.context: Brooks's last letter, in voiceover, explaining his decision to take his own life in the halfway-house room.

quotes.text: Brooks was here.
quotes.speaker: Brooks Hatlen
quotes.context: Brooks's last act before he hangs himself in the halfway-house room is to carve these three words into the rafter above the chair.

quotes.text: Salvation lies within.
quotes.speaker: Warden Norton
quotes.context: Norton handing Andy a Bible during a cell inspection, preaching while he stands beside the very book that hides the rock hammer Andy is using to dig.

quotes.text: I believe in two things. Discipline and the Bible. Here you'll receive both.
quotes.speaker: Warden Norton
quotes.context: Norton's induction speech to the new prisoners, pairing the lash and the scripture as the prison's two operating instruments.

quotes.text: I had to come to prison to be a crook.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy to Red in the yard, after years of laundering Norton's kickbacks under the alias Randall Stephens.

quotes.text: He said he did it, said this hotshot banker took the rap for it.
quotes.speaker: Tommy Williams
quotes.context: Tommy telling Red and Andy in the yard about the cellmate at another prison who confessed to the country-club murder Andy was convicted of.

quotes.text: Elmo Blatch. Big, twitchy bastard.
quotes.speaker: Tommy Williams
quotes.context: Tommy naming the man who confessed to the murder Andy was convicted of, the testimony that triggers Norton's response.

quotes.text: How can you be so obtuse?
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy losing his composure with Norton in the warden's office, when Norton refuses to act on Tommy's testimony.

quotes.text: Andy went into the hole, and Tommy went into the ground.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover summing up the aftermath of Tommy's testimony, pairing Andy's solitary confinement with Tommy's murder in the yard.

quotes.text: Geology is the study of pressure and time. That's all it takes really, pressure, and time.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover, after the escape is revealed, paraphrasing what Andy had told him long before about the slow erosion of stone.

quotes.text: Andy Dufresne, who crawled through a river of shit and came out clean on the other side.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during the escape sequence, as Andy emerges from the sewer pipe into the storm.

quotes.text: Some birds aren't meant to be caged. Their feathers are just too bright.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover, in the days after Andy's escape, reflecting on his friend's absence from Shawshank.

quotes.text: Mr. Stevens enjoys a rather lofty existence. As far as the state police are concerned, he's a ghost.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during the bank-withdrawal montage, framing Andy's alias as the device that empties Norton's accounts.

quotes.text: His judgement cometh and that right soon.
quotes.speaker: Warden Norton
quotes.context: The embroidered sampler hanging behind Norton's desk for the entire film, last seen as Norton sees the troopers crossing the yard and reaches for his revolver.

quotes.text: Rehabilitated? It's just a bullshit word.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red at his fortieth-year parole hearing, abandoning the rehearsed answer he had used at every previous hearing.

quotes.text: I want to talk to him. I want to try and talk some sense to him, tell him the way things are. But I can't. That kid's long gone.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red at his final parole hearing, speaking honestly for the first time about the young man he was when he committed his crime.

quotes.text: This old man is all that's left.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red closing his statement at the final parole hearing, conceding the gulf between the man who entered Shawshank and the man asking to leave it.

quotes.text: Remember, Red, hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy's letter to Red, hidden under the oak tree in the Buxton hayfield, read in voiceover by Red after he digs up the tin.

quotes.text: Get busy living, or get busy dying.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy to Red on the yard bench near the prison wall, the line that returns at the climax in the Buxton letter.

quotes.text: The Pacific Ocean. You know what the Mexicans say about the Pacific? They say it has no memory.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy on the yard bench, telling Red about the Mexican town he plans to live in, the phrase that becomes the closing image of the film.

quotes.text: I find I'm so excited I can barely sit still or hold a thought in my head. I think it's the excitement only a free man can feel.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: The closing lines of Andy's letter to Red, voiced over Red's bus ride south to the border.

quotes.text: I hope I can make it across the border. I hope to see my friend and shake his hand. I hope the Pacific is as blue as it has been in my dreams.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's closing voiceover on the bus south, the film's final lines before the reunion shot on the beach.

quotes.text: I hope.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: The last words of Red's voiceover, and the last spoken words of the film.

quotes.text: My wife used to say I'm a hard man to know. Like a closed book.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy on the yard bench, opening his quietest conversation with Red about the marriage that ended in his conviction.

quotes.text: I didn't pull the trigger, but I drove her away. That's why she died, because of me.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy on the yard bench, telling Red the only honest version of what happened with his wife.

quotes.text: Bad luck, I guess. It floats around. It's gotta land on somebody.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy to Red on the yard bench, accepting the share of responsibility for his wife's death without surrendering his innocence of the murder.

quotes.text: Andy was a quiet kind of guy. There's something inside that they couldn't get to.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover summing up his early years of friendship with Andy, in the lead-up to the Mozart broadcast.

quotes.text: Time draws out like a blade.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during Andy's month in solitary after Tommy's murder.

quotes.text: Pressure and time. That, and a big goddamn poster.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover after the escape is revealed, condensing the means of Andy's freedom into a single line.

quotes.text: I find I am so excited I can barely sit still.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red echoing the closing line of Andy's letter as he rides the bus toward the border, his voiceover crossing into the same words he has just read.

quotes.text: I hope.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's final voiceover word held over the long pull-back over the Pacific.

quotes.text: If it takes longer, I'll write four letters a week instead of one.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy in his early library years, replying to Red's scepticism about whether the state senate will ever fund a prison library.

quotes.text: All it took was pressure and time. And a few hundred letters.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover paraphrasing Andy's library campaign, after the state finally caves and sends the books.

quotes.text: I'd appreciate it if you'd grade his test.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy retrieving Tommy's discarded GED paper from the rubbish bin in the library and posting it for grading without telling him.

quotes.text: He passed by a C-plus average. Thought you'd like to know.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy in voiceover via letter, telling Tommy he had passed his GED.

quotes.text: It's a funny thing. On the outside I was an honest man. Straight as an arrow. I had to come to prison to be a crook.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: Andy to Red in the yard, summing up his years as Norton's accountant.

quotes.text: Lord, the man's a tightwad.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover on Norton's Inside Out programme, framing the warden's public morality as a thin cover over private avarice.

quotes.text: I have no idea to this day what those two Italian ladies were singing about. Truth is, I don't want to know.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during the Mozart broadcast, refusing to translate the moment.

quotes.text: Some things are best left unsaid. I'd like to think they were singing about something so beautiful it can't be expressed in words.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover continuing his reflection on the Mozart broadcast, framing the music as transcending the institution that briefly carries it.

quotes.text: And makes your heart ache because of it.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover finishing his reflection on the Mozart broadcast, the line that ends the sequence.

quotes.text: Norton's a hypocrite. There are no two ways about it.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover during a montage of Norton's public sermons and private kickbacks, summing up the warden in plain terms.

quotes.text: Tommy was a good kid. Smart kid, when he wanted to be.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover after Tommy passes the GED, framing the murder that follows as the loss of someone the prison had begun to redeem.

quotes.text: I'd like to think the last thing that went through his head, other than that bullet, was to wonder how the hell Andy Dufresne ever got the best of him.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover over the troopers escorting Hadley out of the prison and Norton's body slumped in the office chair.

quotes.text: I have to remind myself that some birds aren't meant to be caged.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover at the close of the escape sequence, framing Andy's absence as a kind of release for everyone who knew him.

quotes.text: And the part of you that knows it was a sin to lock them up does rejoice.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover after the escape, completing the bird metaphor as the camera pans Andy's now-empty cell.

quotes.text: Still, the place you live in is that much more drab and empty that they're gone.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover finishing the bird metaphor, registering the cost to those left behind.

quotes.text: I guess I just miss my friend.
quotes.speaker: Red
quotes.context: Red's voiceover as the bird metaphor closes, the line that anchors the rest of the film toward the reunion in Mexico.

quotes.text: Dear Red. If you're reading this, you've gotten out.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: The opening line of Andy's letter under the oak tree in the Buxton hayfield, voiced over the moment Red unfolds the page.

quotes.text: And if you've come this far, maybe you're willing to come a little further.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: From Andy's letter under the oak, framing the journey south as the next step rather than the last.

quotes.text: I will be hoping that this letter finds you, and finds you well.
quotes.speaker: Andy Dufresne
quotes.context: From Andy's letter under the oak in Buxton, the closing courtesy before the famous lines about hope.
